clue.text: Being angelic, keep quiet about cut-back

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other, so the hush surrounds the trimmed word

parts.note: SH is the call for someone to keep quiet

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is read the other way round

parts.note: to cut is to pare

explanation.surface: A heavenly creature is told to stay silent about some cut-back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being angelic' looks like a description, but the whole phrase is the definition: a being that is angelic.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest orders of angels, a heavenly creature.

clue.text: Litter stuck in the wall

definitions.meaning: a litter is a frame for carrying the sick
a brick laid lengthwise along the face of a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher carries the injured, and in bricklaying it is a brick set with its long side showing.

clue.text: Works out right — no capsizing in rough seas

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the shuffled letters
rough seas are churned up, so the letters of seas are rearranged
a capsizing boat turns over, so the word no is turned round

explanation.surface: A sailor calculates the right course, with no chance of overturning in heavy water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizing' turns the word no round, 'rough' shuffles seas, and 'in' sets the turned word inside the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason something out is to work it out by logical thought.

clue.text: Highly esteemed holding company that's far ahead of others

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second

parts.note: precious means greatly valued

explanation.surface: A prestigious firm stays well in front of its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A precocious child is advanced for its age, developed beyond its peers.

clue.text: Stage craft on the home front

definitions.text: Stage craft on the home front

parts.words: Stage craft on the home front
parts.note: A Gilbert and Sullivan operetta about a ship, a craft on stage; the same word is an apron worn at the front while doing housework

explanation.surface: Theatrical skill displayed in wartime domestic life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage craft' reads as theatrical skill but means a ship in a stage show: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless apron covering the front of a dress, worn for housework, and also the ship in the operetta title.

clue.text: Broke a sign, perhaps — and audacious about it

indicators.note: about means the cheeky word goes around the sign letter

parts.note: insolent means cheeky and audacious
the V-sign is a rude hand gesture, an example of a sign

explanation.surface: Someone smashed a road sign and was cheeky about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' reads as smashed but means penniless. A V-sign is a rude British gesture, two fingers raised.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay debts, out of money.

clue.text: A mother can be the making of a man

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, such as a horse

explanation.surface: A mother's influence can turn a boy into a man.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Adam is the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam is the first man in the Bible, so a man by name.

clue.text: Letters dispatched in settlement

parts.note: letters sent out are dispatched
post is letters and mail

explanation.surface: Mail is sent to a far-flung colony.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote settlement or station far from the centre.

clue.text: A listening device, this is dropped in a fox-hole

parts.note: an ear is the organ of hearing

indicators.note: is dropped means the letters i and s are taken out of this

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bug is planted in a hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listening device' suggests a bug, but it is the ear; 'is dropped' takes IS out of THIS to leave TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox lives in an underground burrow, its den.

clue.text: A large animal, yet among the most agile

indicators.note: among says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A big creature, yet one of the nimblest.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is a large animal.

clue.text: Respecting a representative employed by chemists

parts.note: re means respecting, concerning, as in business letters
an agent is a representative acting for someone

explanation.surface: Concerning a sales rep who has been hired by pharmacists.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used in a chemical reaction, a tool of laboratory work.

clue.text: Go to pieces when threats are made

indicators.note: the letters of threats are made into something new, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone cracks up when menaced.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into fragments, just as something falling apart does.

clue.text: All out, even if not very well

parts.note: tho is an informal spelling of though, meaning even if
roughly means approximately, done without much care or precision

explanation.surface: Completely exhausted, even if not seriously unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Going all out means doing something completely, with total effort.

clue.text: See small church and large stretch of water North of the Border

definitions.text: large stretch of water North of the Border

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A tourist looks at a chapel and a great Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the Border' means in Scotland, the border being the one with England.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is the Scottish word for a lake or sea inlet.

clue.text: The reason for getting lost?

parts.note: plays on the proverb that he who wavers is lost, rather than someone losing their way

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'he who hesitates is lost' makes delay the cause of being lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation is pausing in doubt, which the proverb blames for losing out.

clue.text: Opposed mistreatment of the soil

indicators.note: mistreatment suggests the letters of the phrase are mishandled into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer objected to the poor handling of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile describes being against something, unfriendly or antagonistic.

clue.text: He's antagonised Oriental holy man and guide

parts.note: E, east, stands for oriental
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
a ranger guides visitors through a park or forest

explanation.surface: A man has been upset by an Eastern sage and his escort.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'He's antagonised' as 'he has antagonised': one who alienates others.
explanation.definitionFit: An estranger is one who drives others away, making former friends hostile.

clue.text: The person raising a point with the minister

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
a rector is a parish clergyman, a minister

explanation.surface: Someone brings up an issue with the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising a point' reads as making an argument, but 'The person raising' is the definition and the point is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is one who puts something up, builds or lifts it.

clue.text: Dire scene created in the home

indicators.note: created suggests the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A terrible row breaks out at the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling, the place where one lives.

clue.text: Detail soldiers to accompany foreign nobility

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps of soldiers
a count is a continental nobleman, the equivalent of an earl

explanation.surface: An officer assigns troops to escort a visiting aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' looks like the military verb, assign to a duty, but means to tell in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount is to narrate or relate in detail.

clue.text: Song — "Many an Adieu"

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye

explanation.surface: A song title about saying lots of goodbyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a vocal composition for singers and orchestra.

clue.text: Sports guns used after the end of August

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: rifles are guns

explanation.surface: Shooting parties take up their guns once the month of August is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used after' puts the gun word after the final letter of August.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy or play with it, so trifles here means plays idly.

clue.text: A story about bovine creatures being ruled

indicators.note: about means the fib goes around the cattle

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib
neat is an old word for cattle

explanation.surface: A tale about cattle being kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineate means marked with lines, as ruled paper is.

clue.text: Waste wood

definitions.meaning: the timber of a coniferous tree

explanation.definitionFit: Pining means wasting away with grief, and the timber is a common softwood.

clue.text: Newspaper drive?

explanation.definitionFit: The press means journalism and newspapers, and to press is to drive or push hard.

clue.text: Kept a man tied in possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A man was held captive, perhaps tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintained means kept up or preserved in good order.

clue.text: People of some standing — they can open doors, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals the sound of a word

parts.note: door knobs are turned to open doors

explanation.surface: Important people are rumoured to have access everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they can open doors' suggests influence, but means door handles.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobs is British slang for wealthy or upper-class people.

clue.text: A thinker to pay attention to

definitions.meaning: a great intellect can be called a fine ...
to heed or look after something

explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant person is a great intellect, and to look out for is to heed.

clue.text: Making a cancellation — time to give voice!

parts.note: an era is a period of time
to sing is to give voice in song

explanation.surface: A concert is called off just as it is the singer's moment to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasing is rubbing out or deleting, a kind of cancelling.

clue.text: 26 holds it to be a great country

indicators.note: holds means the first word contains the second

parts.note: the answer to 26 down is mind, another word for brain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker believes a nation to be great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds it to be' reads as 'believes', but 'holds' is the container signal and 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Britain is the island nation of England, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: Sort of tree to set by a highway

parts.note: to stand something is to set it upright
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Planting instructions say to put a tree by the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a tree or shrub grown with a tall single stem and no lower branches.

clue.text: Stick given as trendy present

parts.note: in means fashionable
here means present, as at a roll call

explanation.surface: A walking cane is handed over as a fashionable gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a cane and 'present' a gift; both are misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to exist as an essential part, to stay fixed within something.
